transcript.text: Thank you, Morgan, for sharing your perspective and for taking responsibility for the interruptions. I appreciate that your account aligns with what I observed. Let me now walk through the four specific incidents as Dana requested. Incident one: I was presenting a project timeline update to the group when Morgan cut in mid-sentence to question the feasibility of a milestone date. I clarified that the date was based on stakeholder confirmation, and Morgan acknowledged that and revised the question to ask about contingency planning instead. Incident two: A colleague was presenting a status update on their workstream when Morgan interrupted to flag a dependency risk. The colleague clarified that the dependency had already been flagged in the shared tracker, and Morgan accepted that and adjusted to ask how the mitigation was progressing. Incident three: I was speaking about a design decision when Morgan cut over me to raise an alternative approach. I clarified that the alternative had already been evaluated and ruled out in a prior discussion, and Morgan accepted that context and revised the suggestion to build on the chosen approach instead. Incident four: During a brainstorming segment, Morgan interrupted me while I was outlining a proposal to point out a potential gap. I clarified that the gap was addressed in a later section of the proposal, and Morgan acknowledged that and refocused on the section at hand. In all four cases, the course-correction was genuine and the discussion continued productively afterward. My recommendation remains the same — a facilitated repair meeting between Morgan and me, combined with Lee's mentoring check-ins, as a constructive developmental path forward. I don't believe formal discipline is warranted.
